analysis.title: 'Doves' Drive Oil & Rate-Hike Odds Down; Dollar & Gold Bid Ahead Of Macro/Micro Maelstrom
key_insights: Stocks, bonds and oil moved independently on Sep 29 after tracking each other tick for tick the day before. Dovish Fed talk (Williams), Qatar mediation talk and a Trump meeting with tech CEOs offset selling pressure. Only the Nasdaq 100 gained, small caps lagged most, and the S&P 500 and Dow closed lower.

NY Fed President Williams said one more rate hike late this year may be appropriate but there is no urgency after the September hike. October hike odds had risen to 75% during the prior week's hawkish Fed talk and fell back to pre-hawk, pre-ISM levels.
The 2-year yield fell 4bps and the 30-year rose 5bps, steepening the curve back to pre-FOMC levels. The 30-year topped 5.61% on Tuesday, a level last seen in 2002.

Long-end Treasuries are pressured by inflation worries (ISM Prices Paid), heavy corporate supply and AI capex funding. Paramount Skydance began a roughly $32B investment-grade sale, part of a $52B debt package for Warner Bros. Discovery, and SMBC called it the fifth-largest IG deal on record. Citigroup describes a 'light buyer's strike' in Treasuries.

Treasuries have posted a median loss of 0.9% in September and 0.7% in October over the past decade (Bloomberg). This September is the worst since 2023. TD Securities says the pain trade may continue and could spread to equities without a Middle East resolution.

WTI front-month fell more than 3% to below $90, helped by Qatar saying mediators are still passing messages between Iran and the US, Saudi Arabia restoring about half of its East-West pipeline capacity, the IEA saying it is ready to act, and up to 40 million more barrels offered from the US SPR. Reported US support for easing Russia sanctions also weighed on crude. Futures were affected by a contract roll.

Physical oil remains tight. Dated Brent is at $120 and the WTI cash roll is at extreme levels. Iran reportedly struck a VLCC in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, and Iran's parliament speaker warned that if Iran's security is not ensured, no infrastructure will be safe.

Goldman's Rich Privorotsky sees the US and Iran inching closer to a deal, calling reports of US openness to sanctions relief a trial balloon, while noting the risk of miscalculation is large. Bloomberg's Frank Monkam says October could bring peak pressure from Iran before the US midterms remove its supply-crisis leverage.
Privorotsky says the speed of the rise in real rates is becoming too punitive for stocks to ignore. Bond volatility is soaring while equity volatility stays complacent.

AI news dominated equities. Sonnet 5.5 is described by Goldman as near Opus level on some benchmarks, more than 30% faster than Sonnet 5 and materially cheaper than Opus. OpenAI's Astra update has been pulled back after alignment and security issues. OpenAI DevDay is Sep 30, with an always-on agent expected. Oracle rose as much as 8.2% on a report that OpenAI annual recurring revenue is nearing $70B.
BofA warned that AI agents, especially Meta's Muse, could pull shopping, forms and checkout off Apple devices and services. Mag7 lagged the S&P 493 and AI-linked stocks outperformed non-AI.

Market breadth is weak. NYSE new lows exceeded new highs for the tenth straight day, the NYSE Composite is at 3-month lows, and the median stock is well off its highs. Momentum stocks rallied 11 straight days, with Goldman's momentum basket up 28% in September, its best month since June 2000.

Goldman's trading desk rated activity 2 out of 10 with the floor 3% net sellers. Long-only clients are better sellers with supply in info tech, consumer discretionary and healthcare. Hedge funds are better sellers with supply in communication services and industrials, and demand in healthcare.

The dollar rallied to the top of its 17-month channel. Gold rebounded modestly off the prior day's plunge lows. Bitcoin closed unchanged, and Glassnode says it is up 35% from the August low while coin-denominated open interest is down almost 20% to its lowest since March.

Seasonality may be turning. The worst half-month of the year is nearly over, JPMorgan's traders are 'tactically bullish', and the first half of October has one of the year's best hit-rates, including in midterm years. The week's catalysts are Micron, Accenture and Nike results, then PCE, ISM and payrolls.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Privorotsky sees the sides inching closer, with mediators active, Trump expecting more talks this week and incentives pointing toward a deal. Saudi pipeline flows and IEA/SPR support add supply relief.
tension_points.bear_case: Iran struck a VLCC in Hormuz and threatens infrastructure, dated Brent remains at $120, and October may bring peak Iranian pressure before the midterms.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A resumption of strikes on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, or talks failing to produce a breakthrough this week.

tension_points.bear_case: Heavy corporate supply, inflation worries and the October seasonal test keep pressure on, and TD sees a continuing pain trade if there is no Middle East resolution.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The 30-year yield continuing higher without value buyers appearing, with losses extending into October.
